changes.summary: Flash-Next DFlash2 launch profile and setup candidate: separate incoai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DFlash2 draft, FR-Spec 65,536-ID map, resident rowwise-FP8 output head reuse, 0.95 memory fraction for image-workload headroom, 6 requests / 36 Mamba slots, 524,288-token context, 2,048-token draft window, HiCache/NIXL unchanged; offered as an optional profile — explicit saved selections are preserved.

Verify width is fixed by active concurrency through the bundled fixed policy: block 6 at one running request, block 4 at two or more; one candidate per tier keeps the width stable between boots. Proposal-probability scratch is keyed by width and routing stays valid when a width captures nothing. The 3.0-era SPECULATIVE_NUM_DRAFT_TOKENS setting is retired on this profile.

Native NEXTN MTP verify width is fixed by active concurrency through the bundled fixed policy configs/pennyroyal/adaptive-next.json (SHA-256 3edaa87d66f535caae0bddb8f457f03fce0f6dc1f4e8091b20495a0dc9da41fb, pinned by the recipes): block 8 at one running request, block 4 at two or more; one candidate per tier keeps the width stable between boots. The launch carries the widest routed block (steps 7, draft tokens 8); the acceptance EMA cannot trade widths.

The optional Flash-Next DFlash2 profile now uses FlashInfer for target linear-attention verification (--linear-attn-verify-backend flashinfer); the native recipe and the container startup files select it automatically. On the final source, matched screens show single-request decode at block 6 rising from 227.37 to 241.49 tok/s mean (sampled peak 339.53) and the full six-request batch at block 4 from 503.41 to 504.80 aggregate (peak 568.90).

The beta configurator offers the next-dflash2 profile on the native and container paths, prompts for the draft checkpoint, and carries the fixed-width policy and FlashInfer verification from the samples. External container configuration files and the manual native recipes remain the primary setup paths.

Remove the preset KV-token cap; the engine sizes the shared pool from profiled memory inside the static memory fraction. An explicit MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS remains a deliberate positive, page-aligned override on every profile.
FR-Spec candidate projection for DFlash2 narrows the draft's searched vocabulary while the target keeps full verification.
Support the resident rowwise FP8 output head in DFlash2 so the draft reuses the target's converted head.
Bound draft GPU KV allocation to sliding-window requirements.
Preserve ordinary host HiCache capacity while the draft GPU pool stays bounded.
Flash-Next DFlash2 supports ordinary TP2 capture using the complete replicated hyper-connection state. TP2 is expected to work; it has not been tested on two-GPU hardware.
Drop finished requests from the running batch before every admission and count a request's held req_to_token row once at admission.
Honor stop-regex matches inside accepted speculative blocks on both DFlash2 block sizes.
Prevent the identified scheduler crash when token-probability requests mix with ordinary generation.
Retain the measured .97 memory fraction for the native MTP FR-Spec recipe, separate from the DFlash2 .95 default.
Native NEXTN MTP remains the maintained Flash-Next default for new setups; Flash-Next DFlash2 remains available as an optional profile.

Agreed subset: QSA restore ordering, packed scratch initialization, shared Chat/Responses chat_template trust gate, absent tool-call fields, stream timestamps, malformed-image 400s, collection before KV sizing, existing ignore_eos accounting, freed-response-state handling.
Optional Swift FP8 PLE transplant/verification recipe with whole-data-section, table-width, scale and payload validation; serving qualification remains contributor-owned.

Restore the maintained native NEXTN MTP Flash-Next profile as the default for new setups across the recipes, the container startup defaults and the configurator; next-dflash2 remains fully available as an opt-in and explicit saved selections are preserved.

performance.presentation_detail: Real agentic ten-slide workflow on final source a60f442 at C1 W6 with FlashInfer verification and explicit medium reasoning effort: 70 model turns matched 70 server requests, 1,075 complete decode intervals over 570.391832 s, 132,873 server output tokens including reasoning, prompt growth 42,527 to 206,219 tokens; the workflow completed on the normal presentation tools and the finished deck previewed; total workflow time including tools and rendering was 13 minutes 44 seconds. The earlier five-slide xhigh screen on the Triton verification path (194.56/421.35; 121 turns, 192,349 output tokens, 1,676 intervals over 909.385 s, prompt 42,637 to 253,267, 33 minutes 25 seconds total) is retained as dated history; the runs differ in slide count and effort setting.
performance.coding_flow_note: The medium-effort coding rerun on a60f442 (259.38/439.28) did not complete, and its handoff does not accept it as a new published coding benchmark. The accepted coding-flow timing (235.60/417.50, 5ca3f39, Triton path) remains dated history.
performance.conditions: Native elapsed-weighted complete active-decode intervals and sampled peak from the same window, including reasoning; normal non-greedy sampling (temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, top-k 40, min-p 0.05), 128-token inputs, 1,024-token output ceiling, three repeats at seeds 42, 43 and 44; xhigh reasoning for the matched screens, explicit medium for the ten-slide presentation. Rows keep their recorded source/configuration labels: a60f442 for the native-MTP C1/W8, FlashInfer DFlash2 and presentation screens; 5ca3f39 for the dated fixed-W4 and coding-flow screens; 27f9eaa for the 27B fixed-W8 screens. C4/C6 rows are aggregate over the full running batch, not per-request rates. The native-MTP full-batch screen at the routed W4 width does not exist yet; only its C1/W8 rate is shown, so no native-versus-DFlash2 full-batch comparison is made. The corrected full-batch means supersede the earlier drain-inclusive 522.69/386.26 summaries.
performance.completion_facts: The ten-slide presentation completed end to end on a60f442 with all 70 turns matched one-to-one and the deck previewed; the earlier coding-flow completion fact is recorded in the qualification notes, separate from its accepted timing; the new medium coding rerun is unfinished and not accepted.
performance.hardware_note: All local numbers are one RTX PRO 6000 at TP1; TP2 on the optional DFlash2 profile is expected to work and has not been tested on two-GPU hardware.
